question: What is ikhlas (sincerity) and why is it the foundation of accepted deeds?
summary: Ikhlas (sincerity) means performing all acts of worship and obedience solely for Allah's sake, free from showing off (riya') or seeking worldly benefit. It is the condition without which no deed is accepted, and the Prophet ﷺ described it as the foundation of the religion.
answer:
Ikhlas — sincerity of intention and action for Allah alone — is the most fundamental inner quality in Islam. Without it, no deed has value before Allah, however outwardly perfect it may appear.

**The definition:**
Ikhlas is to direct all acts of worship and obedience solely to Allah, seeking nothing except His pleasure. It is the opposite of riya' (showing off, doing deeds to impress people) and sum'ah (doing deeds to gain reputation).

**The foundation of accepted deeds:**
Allah says: 'So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.' (Quran 18:110). This verse is understood by scholars as requiring two conditions for an accepted deed: being in accordance with the Sunnah (righteous deed) and being solely for Allah (ikhlas).

Ibn al-Qayyim said: 'A deed without ikhlas is like a traveller who fills his bag with gravel — it burdens him but does not benefit him.'

**The first person on the Day of Judgment:**
The Prophet ﷺ narrated that among the first people whose case will be settled on the Day of Resurrection will be a scholar, a martyr, and a charitable person — all of whom will be thrown into the Fire because they did their deeds not for Allah but for worldly reputation. (Sahih Muslim 1905 — one of the most sobering hadith in the collection).

**Surah al-Ikhlas and its name:**
The name of Surah 112 (Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad) is al-Ikhlas — affirming the absolute oneness of Allah. This surah is the foundation of ikhlas in aqeedah: Allah is One, Eternal, uncreated, without equal. Worshipping Him with ikhlas means directing all worship to this Being alone.

**Levels of ikhlas:**
1. **General ikhlas:** Doing the deed for Allah, not people.
2. **Complete ikhlas:** Not even noticing whether people observe the deed or not.
3. **Perfect ikhlas:** The degree described by Imam al-Ghazali — performing the deed as if in the presence of Allah, with no awareness of anything else.

**Riya' (showing off):**
The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The thing I fear most for you is minor shirk.' They asked: 'What is minor shirk?' He said: 'Riya' — showing off. Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: "Go to those you were showing off for in the world, and see if you find any reward with them."' (Musnad Ahmad 23630 — graded sahih by al-Albani)

**How to cultivate ikhlas:**
Scholars identify: frequent renewing of intention before deeds, avoiding speaking about one's deeds unless necessary, being equally diligent in private and public worship, and seeking forgiveness when one notices riya' entering a deed.
evidence_quran: 18:110 — 'Let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in worship of his Lord'
98:5 — 'They were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion'
39:11 — 'I was commanded to worship Allah with sincere dedication'
evidence_hadith: Sahih Muslim 1905 — The scholar, martyr, and charitable person who did their deeds for reputation are thrown into the Fire — the most powerful warning against riya'
Musnad Ahmad 23630 — Riya' is minor shirk (graded sahih by al-Albani)
Sahih Bukhari 54 / Sahih Muslim 1907 — 'Actions are only by intentions, and every person will have only what they intended.'
scholar_consensus: Ikhlas is a condition of accepted worship in all four schools. Riya' (showing off) renders deeds valueless and is described as minor shirk. All schools emphasise ikhlas as the internal foundation that validates external action.

madhab_positions.hanafi: Ikhlas is required for the validity of worship in the Hanafi tradition. Intentions must be renewed and purified. Imam Abu Hanifa said: 'Whoever seeks worldly benefit through his deeds of deen has destroyed his deen.'
madhab_positions.maliki: Imam Malik is reported to have said: 'Ikhlas is that you do not desire any witnesses to your deed other than Allah.' Maliki scholars emphasise the purification of the nafs (soul) as a prerequisite for sustained ikhlas.
madhab_positions.shafii: Imam al-Shafi'i: 'I wish that people would learn this knowledge [fiqh] without attributing any of it to me' — a demonstration of ikhlas. Shafi'i scholars have an extensive tradition in the purification of intentions.
madhab_positions.hanbali: Ibn al-Qayyim wrote perhaps the most extensive Islamic treatment of ikhlas and its relationship to accepted worship in 'Madarij al-Salikin.' The Hanbali tradition treats ikhlas as inseparable from correct aqeedah and worship.

disclaimer: This is a study reference based on classical sources. Ikhlas is an interior matter that only Allah sees fully. For guidance on spiritual development and purification of intention, seek a qualified scholar or teacher.
